thread.title: Apple plans to launch streaming service globally early next year

author: Annlee Ellingson
title: Apple plans to launch streaming service globally early next year
text: – Staff Writer, L.A. Biz Oct 23, 2018, 2:49pm PDT Apple Inc. may be late to the streaming game, but when the computer giant does launch its video platform, it plans to take it global. The company aims to launch its streaming service in more than 100 countries, reported The Information . By comparison, both Netflix and Amazon’s streaming platforms are available in about twice as many countries. Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL) plans to launch its streaming service in the United States in the first half of next year, sources told the tech news site, and expand it internationally in the following months. The platform will include original programming from Apple as well as the ability to sign up for subscription channels from other companies, a la Amazon Channels. Earlier this month it was reported that Apple plans to put the service on its iPhones, iPads and Apple TVs in the preinstalled “TV” app. Owners of such devices will be able to watch Apple’s original content for free . Apple has committed an initial $1 billion to content for the initiative, which has signed content deals with Oprah Winfrey and Sesame Workshop and is working on series including “Amazing Stories,” a drama about a morning new show starring Jennifer Aniston, Reese Witherspoon and as of this week Steve Carell, and a thriller from M. Night Shyamalan, among other projects. Apple’s worldwide video programming is led by Jamie Erlicht and Zack Van Amburg, whom the company poached from Sony last year. Under their leadership, Sony Pictures Television produced such hits as “The Blacklist” for NBC, “The Goldbergs” for ABC, and “Kevin Can Wait” for CBS, as well as cable shows “Breaking Bad” and its spinoff “Better Call Saul” for AMC and “Outlander” for Starz, and digital series “The Crown” and “Bloodline” for Netflix and “Sneaky Pete” for Amazon.
